implementation_decisions: Emit exactly one terminal row for each closed or EOF-flushed TCP/UDP flow generation.
Keep legacy feature indices 0 through 53 unchanged and append terminal features at indices 54 through 69.
Keep identifiers, capture and dataset origin, raw IPs, absolute timestamps, labels, schedules, exact close reason, and partition out of model input.
Use causal first-packet context, first-observed ports, and a coarse exhaustive lifecycle one-hot.
Export the five PCAP inputs offline before adding live DPDK terminal inference.
Split by capture-aware groups; fit preprocessing and models on training only; choose thresholds on validation only.
Run native live inference through ONNX Runtime C++ with no Python sidecar.
Prioritize a working FTP-Patator and PortScan vertical slice before extended benchmark or report work.
Model V2 uses a binary Benign/Attack head and a 13-class attack-family head sourced from assigned_class.
Reference feature audit binds the exact physical 70-column Parquet suffix; duplicate names are never selected by name.
Production Model V2 fit and threshold selection remain blocked until a preregistered whole-attempt live split is locked.
The live-split policy is immutable; user-selected required and reserve attempt counts produce a separate deterministic split-lock artifact.
A slot is claimed with create-new semantics before capture; failed or aborted attempts consume their slot and may use only a preregistered reserve.
The Model V2 trainer currently exposes preflight check and label/profile projection only; it has no fit or threshold-selection command.
The user locked required attempts per campaign to train=3, validation=2, holdout=2, with one reserve slot in each partition.
The claim writer derives campaign, partition, and receipt path from an exact required slot; callers provide only the five locked identity scalars.
The claim ledger rejects holdout, reserve, unknown entries, identity reuse, cross-partition sessions, and overwrite attempts before traffic.
Each campaign is bound to an exact attempt-id prefix; the orchestrator must derive and hash the fixed run contract before invoking the path-free public claim API.
Atomic hard-link publication is unit-verified on Windows but remains blocked from live integration until the exact VMware HGFS path passes a bounded capability probe.
The exact split lock still blocks train and validation capture, so the production claim root remains absent.

side_work_t85_f9_replay_evidence.note: Runs alongside T9.1; touches no Model V2 artifact, no training, no threshold. Recorded here because it is the live evidence the dashboard now serves.
side_work_t85_f9_replay_evidence.objective: Replay every model-available CICIDS family through the live DPDK sensor, stream the alerts to the dashboard, and produce an online-vs-offline comparison on a matched sample.
methodology_decisions: Ground truth comes from the scenario pcap manifest (case_id, label, oracle flow_id), not from a 5-tuple lookup into label_row: that lookup collides on 48% of flows.
Online and offline results cannot be joined by 5-tuple: the reconstruction renumbers source ports (0 of 5343 sensor ports appear in the oracle) although IPs are preserved.

Ground-truth labels are read from the manifest rather than a hardcoded table; the oracle writes en-dash labels ("Web Attack – XSS") and a hyphen copy silently scored the three web families as wrong (offline read 9/12 instead of 12/12).
Online and offline accuracy must be reported over the same family set; a 5-of-14 online figure against a 12-of-12 offline figure is not a comparison.

capture_loss_root_cause.symptom: pass r2 recorded packets_seen=4 on 11 of 14 families; the same number on families with nothing in common
capture_loss_root_cause.cause: kali_t85_golden_sender.py set_link() bounced the NIC (down -> mtu -> up) unconditionally immediately before the nine-frame send, and vmnet swallowed roughly the first five frames while the link converged
capture_loss_root_cause.why_it_hid_in_pass_1: six families replayed a full multi-hundred-thousand-packet PCAP, where losing the opening frames does not matter; it only surfaced once every case was normalised to nine frames
fix: set_link() returns early when the MTU and link state already match, and sleeps 2 seconds after any link-up it does perform
run_t85_pending_replays.py parks the Kali data NIC at the replay MTU once via prepare_link(), so the per-replay call is a no-op
an attempt with packets_seen < 9 is retried in a brand new sensor session, up to 3 tries
capture_loss_root_cause.rejected_fix_and_why: Sending the nine frames again into the live sensor was proposed and is wrong. F9 fires once per flow at packet 9, and the replay rewrites only the MAC header, so a second send repeats the same 5-tuple: the engine appends to the flow that already passed its checkpoint, no second alert is produced, and the duplicated packets corrupt packet-count and inter-arrival-time - the very features under investigation for the GoldenEye divergence.

Identical wrongness is the evidence that the transport is faithful: a transport that corrupted features would produce two different kinds of error.

goldeneye_divergence_resolved.question: DoS GoldenEye scored 6.7% online against 100% offline. Which stage caused it?
goldeneye_divergence_resolved.method: scripts/compare_replay_pacing.py compares elapsed time in the source PCAP against elapsed time at the sensor, over the same flows joined by direction-insensitive 5-tuple.
two_corrections_needed_before_the_number: Every family-window sensor run ended with stop_reason=signal, killed at about 180s rather than finishing the PCAP. The source must be truncated to the packet count the sensor actually saw (packets_seen), otherwise the measurement reports the kill, not the pacing.
The source clock is unix epoch and the sensor clock is monotonic; only elapsed values are comparable, each normalised to its own first event.
goldeneye_divergence_resolved.cause: The vmnet path sustains roughly 550-800 packets per second. A family whose capture rate exceeds that is stretched: GoldenEye's 102135 packets span 50.7s in the source and 189.8s at the sensor, so every inter-arrival gap is multiplied by 3.6. F9 reads inter-arrival time, so a fast flood is presented to the model as a slow one - and GoldenEye's dominant confusion is DoS Hulk (3175), another HTTP DoS with a different timing profile.
goldeneye_divergence_resolved.proof_it_is_not_the_model: The same packets replayed offline, with the original timing intact, score 100% at confidence 1.000.
goldeneye_divergence_resolved.earlier_hypothesis_was_backwards: The changelog previously suspected tcpreplay of COMPRESSING time. It stretches it: the sender cannot keep up, rather than running too fast. The root cause (distorted timing features) was right, the direction was wrong.
goldeneye_divergence_resolved.consistency_with_the_nine_frame_result: Not a contradiction. Nine frames never congest the link, so the nine-frame pass agrees with offline and proves the wire is faithful in content and ordering. The pacing measurement proves it is not faithful in throughput under load. Both hold, and together they close the online/offline gap.

correction_2026_08_09.what_was_wrong: The first pacing measurement truncated the source at packets_seen and reported GoldenEye at x0.28, Hulk at x0.36. That charged dropped packets to the clock.
correction_2026_08_09.evidence: port_ipackets 176791 = port_imissed 74656 + packets_seen 102135, exactly, on every family. port_ipackets is what arrived; packets_seen is what survived the RX ring.
correction_2026_08_09.corrected: Source truncated at port_ipackets. GoldenEye x0.55 pacing with 42.2% RX drop; Hulk x0.71 with 46.0%; DDoS x0.77 with 6.4%; ftp-patator x1.00 and ssh-patator x0.99, both with 0.0%.
correction_2026_08_09.which_effect_dominates: RX drop tracks accuracy more closely than pacing does. Zero drop gives 100% on both families that had it; 6.4% gives 83.8%; 42-46% gives the two worst results. The lab ceiling is around 800 packets per second - below it nothing is dropped.
correction_2026_08_09.why_drop_is_worse_than_stretch: A dropped packet does not stretch a flow, it removes a sample. The nine packets F9 scores become nine survivors rather than the flow's first nine, so packet_count and every inter-arrival feature are computed over the wrong set of packets.
correction_2026_08_09.nine_frame_unaffected: port_imissed is 0 on every nine-frame attempt - nine packets never overflow the RX ring. That is why the nine-frame pass agrees with offline, and equally why it does NOT demonstrate the system holds up under real load.

nine_frame_table_completed.result: 10 of 14 families now have a verified nine-frame online alert - every family that can physically be sent. The remaining four are blocked by LRO/TSO jumbo frames in the capture, which is a property of the PCAP, not a measurement.
nine_frame_table_completed.head_to_head: 9 of 10 comparable families agree between online and offline, including two that are wrong in exactly the same way. Up from 5 of 6. The only divergence remains Web Attack - Sql Injection (0.597 offline vs 0.603 online), two adjacent classes swapping order.
nine_frame_table_completed.root_cause_of_the_earlier_failures: Not unexplained DPDK/vmnet RX flakiness. Two orchestration bugs: pkill without sudo never killed the previous sensor, so later attempts could not bind the port; and the sudo fix matched its own ssh command line and killed the collect step, making every attempt report packets_seen=0. Fixed with the bracket pattern [n]ids_dpdk_live. Three of four families then succeeded on try 3 - retries always worked, the earlier passes just never reached a clean third try.
